Former Laredo mayoral candidates JD Gonzalez and Poncho Casso took the stage together after the election to look back on the campaign trail, in a panel called "From Ballot to Backstage: The Truth Behind Laredo's Mayoral Race" at the J.K. Fine Art Gallery, according to KGNS.

Gonzalez described himself as a political rookie who learned as he went, saying, "Oh, man!" when he recalled being thrown into the race without experience as a lawyer or a politician, KGNS reported. Casso described himself as a "truth serum" and not a true politician, saying he does not care what people think of him and wants to talk about what is going on in Laredo, correcting himself when he is wrong.

Both men talked about young people leaving Laredo, blaming a lack of investment in children and opportunity. Gonzalez said, "Our kids don't need another park. Our kids need opportunity, they need infrastructure." Casso said the city is looking for leadership and there is no one to take the reins, so young people end up getting lost, according to KGNS.

Both men also said multiple campaigns reached out to them seeking an endorsement in the runoff, and neither one endorsed anyone. Gonzalez said it "didn't feel right," explaining that he did not want to endorse for money or because the candidate was his friend, KGNS reported.

The mayoral runoff is Saturday, December 12, between District 8 Councilwoman Alyssa Cigarroa, who led the November 3 vote with 40.75%, and incumbent Mayor Dr. Victor Treviño, who finished second with 32.79%, according to KGNS. Early voting for the runoff runs December 1 through December 8.

Sources: KGNS, November 8, 2026.

title: Gonzalez and Casso, out of the mayor's race, reflect on the campaign trail — and say no to runoff endorsements
